items.question: What afflictions are said not to afflict one after offering?
premises: time death fear and similar afflictions are included
items.inference: the offered rite protects from disease time death fear and related afflictions
uncertainties: exact ritual referent of hutvā is not specified in this verse
items.plain_english: Having offered, one is not afflicted by diseases, time, death, fear, and similar afflictions.

items.question: Which chapter of Jayaratha's commentary on the Vamakesvari Mata concludes here?
premises: the colophon names Jayaratha as composer
the work is a commentary on Vamakesvari Mata
items.inference: this passage closes the fifth chapter of that commentary
uncertainties: whether paṭala means chapter or section depends on edition usage
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the commentary on the Sri Vamakesvari Mata composed by Sri Rajanaka Sri Jayaratha.

items.question: How has this been explained and by whom?
premises: the explanation follows the guru's mouth
items.inference: the matter was briefly explained by some according to the guru's teaching
uncertainties: whether kaiścid refers to commentators or students is not explicit
items.plain_english: This has been briefly explained by some as from the guru's mouth.

items.question: By what reason has this been examined by some?
premises: the examination is questioned as to its reason
items.inference: the verse asks what reason motivated some persons to examine this matter
uncertainties: the exact referent of etad depends on preceding context
items.plain_english: By what reason, then, has this been examined by some?

items.question: What happens when intellect is excluded from hearing?
premises: the result is described as gone
items.inference: excluding intellect from hearing leads to a state described as gone
uncertainties: the exact subject of gatam is not stated in this verse
items.plain_english: Through intellect excluded from hearing, it has gone.

items.question: What fault or merit attaches to speaking without examination?
premises: neither fault nor merit is assigned
the statement is emphatic and final
items.inference: speaking without examination carries neither fault nor merit
uncertainties: whether punaḥ qualifies the whole statement or only the second negation is ambiguous
items.plain_english: Without examining, indeed, it is to be spoken: no fault, no merit again.
